children: , the integrated energy powerhouse, jumped approximately 2.1% to $160.03 Monday as Brent crude punched through $90 per barrel. Oil delivered the rally. Washington delivered the warning. Reuters reported that Exxon was excluded from President Donald Trump's Tuesday meeting with refiners as gasoline prices climbed above $4 per gallon.

The freeze-out follows CEO Darren Woods' January claim that Venezuela remains uninvestable under current conditions. Trump fired back by signaling that Exxon could be shut out of the country, while Chevron, Marathon Petroleum and Valero secured seats at Tuesday's meeting. Refining capacity, biofuel mandates and fuel-shipping costs are on the tableand Exxon will not be in the room.

Exxon generated $17.2 billion of free cash flow in its latest quarterly results, so $90 oil adds serious fuel to an already formidable cash engine. But the stock now trades 26.54% above its $126.47 GF Value estimate, leaving the valuation hot and the margin for disappointment thin. Investors are buying the crude surge today; Exxon's political distance from Washington could send the bill tomorrow.

title: Exxon Gains 2% While Washington Leaves It Outside $4 Gas Talks
